conflicts.fact: The 40-price Wakulima maize dataset changes between lessons, so the same data gives different values, ranges and summary statistics
conflicts.versions: Lessons 1 and 2 give a list ranging KSh 86–115 with no repeated pattern of four values. Lesson 3 shows a range of roughly 86–115 but its tally example uses 110 and 125. Lesson 4 gives a list of only four values (98, 105, 112, 120) with frequencies 16, 12, 8, 4 and Σfx=4204. Lesson 5 groups into classes 90–99 to 140–149. Lessons 6 and 7 use prices around Ksh 40–59 and 55–94, with a mean of about 72.7.

conflicts.fact: Arithmetic of the mean of the ungrouped frequency table
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 gives frequencies 16, 12, 8, 4 (total 40) and Σfx=4204. The mean is stated as KSh 105.10, but 4204/40 = 105.1 does not match the values: 98×16+105×12+112×8+120×4 = 1568+1260+896+480 = 4204. This works, but Lesson 4's mode of 98 is 40% (16/40), while the Lesson 1/2 list has 86–115 with no 98 mode, and Lesson 8 says the mean is higher than the median because of a Rift Valley spike, while Lesson 4's data has no such spike.

conflicts.fact: Shape of the distribution and cause of mean vs median
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says the histogram is right-skewed with modal class KSh 100–109 and a tail to 140–149. Lesson 4 has only values up to 120, with mode 98. Lesson 8 attributes the higher mean to a Rift Valley shortage spike.

conflicts.fact: Modal class and ungrouped mode of maize prices
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 gives modal class Ksh 50–59 (Ksh 10 intervals, from 40–49, 50–59). Lesson 7 gives modal class 70–74 (width 5), midpoint 72. Lesson 5 gives modal class 100–109. Lesson 4 gives mode 98.

conflicts.fact: Mean and median values of the maize prices
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 gives mean ≈72.7 and median ≈73.2 KSh, with the median above the mean. Lesson 8 gives mean ≈105.10 and median ≈103, with the mean above the median.

conflicts.fact: Class width and number of classes for the grouped table
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 uses width 10 (six classes) and a width 15 set. Lesson 7 says 8 classes of width 5.

conflicts.fact: Lesson sequence and order of topics
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 histograms say they use the Lesson 3 table. Lesson 6 says the mean, median and mode were already found before grouping, though Lesson 7 first computes grouped central tendency. Lesson 4 refers to the dot-plot preview as Lesson 6, while histograms are in Lesson 5. Lesson 7 says the next lesson covers histograms with unequal class widths, which was already covered in Lesson 5.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 7's model lists a histogram and frequency polygon already built, while Lesson 6 describes the model as containing a stem-and-leaf plot, and no lesson builds a frequency polygon
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6: raw list, stem-and-leaf or ungrouped table, mean/median/mode. Lesson 7: raw list → tally table → histogram → frequency polygon → ungrouped mean/mode/median.

conflicts.fact: Who builds the model and how many predictions on DQB
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 builds an individual baseline map in exercise books. Lesson 2 says the cumulative model is a group poster begun in Lesson 1. Lesson 4 refers to three Lesson 1 predictions on the DQB, while Lesson 1 posts predictions on a board in two columns.
